subject: MAP weekly checkpoint — performance gate and tuning plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP weekly checkpoint — performance gate and tuning plan

Hi Jordan / team,

Quick MAP checkpoint ahead of today's sync (2pm PT). Attached is the raw latency/throughput dump from our latest canary runs against your representative workload (see acme_latency_report_q1.csv). High-level summary up front:

- p50 latency for the 2k token baseline: 110ms (meets target)
- p95 latency: 450ms (above our 300ms internal gate for sustained QPS)
- Max sustained throughput (16-token average prompt): 320 reqs/s on the dedicated pool configuration we tested

We need to decide today which tuning steps to include in the evaluation plan before final close:
1) Kernel-level quantization profile (Rishi) — risk: minor flakiness on dynamic seqs
2) Cache-prefix warmup (Marissa) — should cut p95 for repeated contexts
3) Autoscale policy adjustment for short spikes (Karthik) — affects cost/SLAs

Action items I propose we confirm today and put in the MAP timeline sheet (attached): owners, risk, fallback plan.

Please review the attached CSV and add any immediate red flags before the call.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
m: +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP weekly checkpoint — performance gate and tuning plan

Thanks Markus — quick notes from the perf team after an initial pass on the CSV:

- p95 spike correlated with longer tail sequences (3k+ tokens) in ~12% of traces; these cause KV-cache churn and force full attention passes.
- A quick quantization sweep (fp16->int8 hybrid on attention kernels) showed ~18% p95 improvement but increased token-drop anomalies on ultra-long sequences in 0.5% of runs.
- Suggested immediate next steps (for the evaluation plan):
  * Run focused int8 smoke tests limited to 10% of canary traffic (owner: rishi_malhotra)
  * Add prefix-warm cache layer in front of canary (owner: marissa_cole)
  * Tune autoscale policy: reduce cooldown windows, add proactive buffer at 20% headroom (owner: karthik_iyer)

I'll upload the perf-run-logs.tar.gz to the drive link Markus shared. If we get agreement on the limited int8 sweep, I can kick it off after the call and share incremental results within 24 hours.

-Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP weekly checkpoint — performance gate and tuning plan

Thanks — the p95 lifts are the main concern for our product team. A few notes from our side:

- Our production workload has intermittent long-context billing statements that push to 3k+ tokens; those are high priority to keep sub-400ms p95.
- Procurement asked to avoid any changes that could impact compliance logging during the evaluation window (i.e., no changes that alter telemetry schema).
- We're comfortable with a controlled int8 sweep if you limit it to a canary pool and provide rollback triggers (e.g., token-drop rate > 0.2% triggers immediate rollback).

See you on the call — Jordan
Jordan Li
Principal ML Engineer, Acme Health
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP weekly checkpoint — performance gate and tuning plan (notes + owner assignments)

Notes from today's sync and owners (captured for MAP sheet):

Meeting outcome: proceed with controlled tuning steps before final close; roadblocked items flagged for update in the evaluation plan.

Action items (owners, due dates):
- Int8 canary sweep (limit 10% traffic, rollback on token-drop > 0.2%): owner=rishi_malhotra, due=2027-04-05 18:00 PT, artifact=perf-run-logs.tar.gz
- Prefix-warm cache implementation for repeated contexts (staging rollout): owner=marissa_cole, due=2027-04-06 12:00 PT, artifact=map_action_items_20270404.xlsx
- Autoscale policy tuning (reduce cooldown, add 20% headroom) and cost impact estimate: owner=karthik_iyer, due=2027-04-06 17:00 PT
- Update MAP timeline and risk matrix in Drive (link above): owner=markus_klein, due=2027-04-05 09:00 PT

Next checkpoint: daily rapid sync until we hit p95 < 300ms for representative long-context traces or until Friday 2027-04-09 for go/no-go decision.

Attachments: acme_latency_report_q1.csv, map_action_items_20270404.xlsx, perf-run-logs.tar.gz

-Markus
